title: Global sections of the constructed increasing-tuple sheaf complex
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec} A$ any morphism of schemes, $U:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to X.\mathrm{Opens}$ any finite family, and $G$ any $\mathcal O_X$-module. The global-section complex of $f_*(\operatorname{extend} C(U,G))$ [def-pc-s3-alternating-cech-sheaf-construction] is isomorphic as an integer cochain complex of $A$-modules to the extension of the increasing-tuple section complex [def-sc-alternating-cech-total-complex], with scalars restricted along $A\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ induced by $f$. No affineness, quasi-coherence or covering hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 01FM, 02KG and 02KH; termwise sheaf and affine comparison before cohomology

proof.text: For each open W, factor the intersection functor V ↦ V ∩ W as inverse image under W → X followed by the open-image functor. Both functors are continuous for the opens sites. Identify the underlying abelian-group intersection presheaf with this composite applied to G; Mathlib Functor.op_comp_isSheaf gives its sheaf condition. PresheafOfModules.isSheaf_of_isLimit gives the sheaf condition of the tuple product, including empty products. Apply Adjunction.isIso_unit_app_of_iso to the actual module sheaf formed by this presheaf to prove that its sheafification unit is an isomorphism. No witness of an unproved existence statement is used.

Evaluate the explicit presheaf product at top using PreservesProduct.iso, map each factor along top ∩ W = W, and apply ModuleCat.piIsoPi. Prove compatibility with a face restriction by presheaf functoriality and uniqueness of opens morphisms. Project each differential to a tuple coordinate; expand the finite signed sum, use this face compatibility, and use additivity of evaluation. HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents forms the nonnegative section-complex isomorphism. The evaluated sheafification unit is natural and has invertible degree components, giving the comparison from sheaf sections to the explicit section complex.

Construct a natural isomorphism between pushforward followed by moduleSpecΓFunctor and top evaluation followed by restriction of scalars along ΓSpecIso.inv ≫ f.appTop: the section maps are identities and their scalar actions agree definitionally. Construct the isomorphism commuting any zero-preserving functor with extension from natural to integer degrees: in nonnegative degree use mapIso of extendXIso; in negative degree both terms are zero and their maps are unique. Check the differential equation with extend_d_eq in nonnegative degrees and IsZero.eq_of_src or eq_of_tgt otherwise. Map the nonnegative comparison through extension and restriction of scalars and compose these isomorphisms.
